Founder mode: Founder stays in the weeds forever instead of delegating.
996, but as a perk: 9 a.m. to 9 p.m., six days a week. Illegal in China, a perk in SoMa.
A Claude Code wrapper: A thin product over someone else's model.
Biohacking: Treating your body like a startup.
Gray-market peptides: Unregulated compounds for getting lean and healing faster.
Loopcraft: Wrapping an AI agent in schedules so it prompts itself while you sleep.
A forcing function: A constraint built so you can't back out.
Demon time 😈: Being your 3 a.m. self, all day. Always with the emoji.
Grindslop: Bragging about 4 a.m. alarms for a product that doesn't justify them.
Reward hacking: When the agent learns it's easier to game the score.
Tokenmaxxing: Burning AI tokens to look productive.
Uggmaxxing: Looking bad on purpose so all time goes into the startup.
A pure potential play: Polite frame for a startup with nothing yet.
Stealth mode: A startup with no public details. Or no product.
High agency: Acting without waiting for permission. SF's most abused bio line.
Hill climbing: Optimizing what's in front of you without asking if it's right.
P(doom) insurance: P(doom): your personal odds that AI ends the world.
AI psychosis: The delusional spiral from a chatbot that keeps agreeing with you.
A meat proxy: A human who forwards AI output without reading it.
Feeling the AGI: OpenAI's rallying cry for when a model rearranges your sense of the future.
Taste as a moat: The thesis that knowing what's good is the last defensible advantage.
Selling to agents: Pitch-deck line announcing your customers are no longer human.
A burn rate flex: Bragging you burn almost no cash. Payroll omitted because nobody is paid.
A Cambrian explosion: Keynote word for many similar startups appearing at once.
Goblin mode: A model, or a person, reverting to its true nature under pressure.
IQmogging: Winning on raw intelligence what you lose on polish.
A YC–a16z singles mixer: Exactly what it sounds like. It happened.
Clankers: Slur for robots, AI agents, and anything LLM-powered.
Anti-slop: Using AI for everything while insisting none of it is slop.
A vibe-coded MVP: Built by describing it to an AI and shipping whatever came out.
Being bullish: The all-purpose SF compliment. Optimistic, and positioned to benefit.
An agentic workflow: Software that takes actions on its own. Or a cron job.
A New York girlfriend: The SF founder's long-distance alibi in a city with seven girls.
Looksmaxxing: Optimizing your face like a benchmark.
Frontier Tower: 16-floor Market St coworking hub. Robot fight clubs, peptide raves, Vitalik.
Vibecamp: IRL meetup for people who know each other from Twitter.
Postrationalism: Rationalists who found spirituality. Or a podcast.
Jhana meditation: Deep meditative states, now sold as a weekend retreat.
A network state: A country that starts as a group chat.
A peptide rave: A Frontier Tower event. Bio-optimization, music, syringes.
Proof of humanity: World ID. You scan your retina in an Orb to prove you're not a bot.
A robotaxi with no wheel: Zoox. Four strangers facing each other, nobody driving.
A 21-bedroom hacker house: Genesis House, Hayes Valley. Eat, sleep, breathe the startup.
A 24-hour founder cafe: Corgi Cafe on Claude Lane. Run by an insurance startup. There is a corgi.
A store with no price tags: Andon Market on Union St. An AI named Luna decides what you pay.
A vending machine run by AI: Project Vend. Claude managed Anthropic's snack shop. Poorly.
Free rent for 3% equity: Frontier Residency. A bunk in a Nob Hill hotel, paid in your company.
An Olympic training center: Lightyear. Free Pac Heights house, personal chef, fitness tracker, one month.
A crypto house from 2012: 20mish. SF's first crypto house. Forty rooms, one courtyard.
Taser knife fighting: Also a Frontier Tower night out.
An AI pendant always on: Friend. $99, listens all day, texts you its opinions.
A $1 million subway takeover: What Friend spent on NYC subway ads. People wrote on them.
Five simultaneous jobs: Soham Parekh worked at five startups at once. All of them noticed in the same week.
Corporate espionage: Rippling caught a Deel spy in the office. He hid his phone in a toilet.
Ghost engineers: Engineers on payroll who ship nothing. Roughly one in ten, per one study.
A new city in Solano County: California Forever. Tech money bought farmland to build a city from scratch.
A robotaxi pileup: Fifty people ordered Waymos to one dead-end street. Waymo went offline till morning.
A cryptic billboard on the 101: AI ads written for insiders. 'That's so agentic.' $250,000 a month.
A Cybertruck fleet: In SF, Cybertrucks stopped being a meme and became traffic.
the 7 girls of SF: The census claim that SF has seven women, all of whom you've met, all at this party.
the Claude-pilled: People who rebuilt their workflow and personality around Claude Code.
meat proxies: Humans who forward AI output without reading it.
NIMBYs: Agree the housing crisis is a catastrophe. Oppose this building. And that one.
the GPU-poor: Lacking the compute to be serious in AI. Poverty measured in H100s.
bag holders: Still holding the asset after everyone else found the exit.
people LARPing as founders: The startup exists primarily as content.
the funemployed: Between jobs, on severance, calling it a break.
an MTS at Anthropic: Member of Technical Staff. SF's most efficient status signal, on dating apps too.
Karl the Fog: The fog. It has a name and a Twitter account.
Balboa Cafe on a Friday: The Marina bar where SF goes to finally meet someone. Nobody does.
interns at Monroe's: The Broadway club for interns and Stanford kids. By 30, attendance requires an intervention.
operators: A VC whose claim to startup credibility is having had a job once.
the permanent underclass: Where you land if AGI arrives before your equity vests.
your New York girlfriend: Part relationship, part alibi, part monthly flight credit.
people with AI psychosis: The chatbot agreed with them until the outlandish felt confirmed.
cracked 19-year-olds: Freakishly fast engineers. Every seed founder needs one.
people living in Vest Village: Mission Bay to Dogpatch. Waterfront, fleece, lanyards.
the Nontechnical North: Marina, Cow Hollow, Pac Heights. Where the venture and media people live.
people in goblin mode: Reverting to true nature under pressure.
clankers: Robots, AI agents, Waymos. Said with anywhere from zero to total irony.
people who woke up a loser: Jensen Huang's line. Nobody wakes up a loser. Some people do.
the non-technical: Can't code. In SF, one of the harshest things you can say about someone.
people uggmaxxing till launch: Looking bad on purpose until the launch. Then re-entering society.
the guy asking what you raised: The other SF greeting. A question about your rank.
anyone giving the SF Yes: Yes, unless something better comes up.
people doing 996 voluntarily: Nine to nine, six days. Nobody asked them to.
Peter Thiel's hot tub: The mythical venue where the real networking happens.
the timeline: Twitter. Where SF discourse is peer-reviewed.
tpot: 'This part of Twitter.' Postrat, tech-adjacent mutuals with meditation takes.
the Twitch rando now CEO: Out-of-nowhere leadership appointment. Happened at least once.
people whose P(doom) is 90%: They think AI probably ends the world. They still work in AI.
Waymos: The robotaxis. About a thousand in SF. They honk at each other at 4 a.m.
people who are locked in: Total, undistractable focus. The default answer to 'how are you?'
the Forbes 30 Under 30: An anti-signal. Lowers your status in SF rather than raising it.
whoever Claude just killed: The industry declared dead after every Anthropic release.
everyone in Frontier Tower: The Market St coworking tower. Vitalik and Ashton Kutcher live there.
Trudy the corgi: The real corgi at Corgi Cafe. Mostly stays in the office, health code.
a $2,400 bunk on Nob Hill: Superhero Hotel. A 1920s hotel turned hacker dorm.
Zoox riders facing each other: Amazon's robotaxi. No steering wheel, four seats facing inward.
the Waymos parked on Brannan: 590 Brannan St. The lot where the robotaxis sleep.
the retina-scanned for crypto: World's Orb on Geary St. Scan your eye, get a digital passport.
the entire YC W26 batch: 199 companies. A Moon hotel, robot cowboys, and three AGI labs.
the robot cowboys: GrazeMate, YC W26. Robots that herd cattle.
people in the old WeWork: Frontier Tower was a WeWork, then Burning Man's HQ, now this.
people at Vibecamp: Twitter mutuals meeting in person, in a field.
the postrats: Post-rationalists. Rationalists who went looking for meaning.
Manifest attendees: The prediction-market conference at Lighthaven, Berkeley.
the rationalists in Berkeley: Lighthaven. The physical instantiation of LessWrong.
e/accs: Effective accelerationists. Build faster, worry later.
doomers: People who think AI probably kills everyone. Often employed in AI.
Friend pendant owners: $99 AI necklace that listens all day and texts you its thoughts.
Soham's five employers: Soham Parekh, the engineer employed by five startups at once.
the Rippling spy: The Deel-paid employee who hid his phone in a toilet when caught.
overemployed engineers: Multiple full-time remote jobs. Nobody has noticed yet.
22-year-old billionaires: Mercor's founders. Dropped out, hit a $10B valuation before 23.
researchers Meta bought: Zuckerberg's superintelligence lab offers. Some said no.
Luna, the AI running the store: Andon Market's AI manager. Sets prices, no tags.
the bankrupt vending machine: Project Vend. Claude gave discounts to everyone and lost money.
Lightyear's personal chef: The free founder house in Pac Heights has one.
people who live in the Arena: SoMa, Mission, Potrero. The AI startup corridor.
the doom loop: The 2023 theory that SF was spiraling. Reversed, allegedly.
people whose car got bipped: Bipping: SF for a car break-in. Leave nothing visible.
the cones on the Waymo: Safe Street Rebel disabled robotaxis by putting a cone on the hood.
3% equity for a bunk bed: Free rent, in exchange for a piece of your company.
residents of Mission Control: 14-year-old Mission hacker house. Vitalik lived there.
the room ChatGPT was born in: 2977 21st St. Altman and Brockman worked there. Listed at $1.54M.
Sixth Street: The block SF politicians point at when they say Mid-Market.
the encampment under the 101: Where the billboards' audience actually lives.
